---
name: team-changes
description: >-
  Use when checking the owner's followed sports teams (pro or college, any
  sport) and their chosen X accounts for what changed since the last check:
  injuries and availability, roster moves, ranking and standings changes. Report
  only changes, tagged official, reported or unknown, each with a source link.
---
# Team changes check

Goal: for each team the owner follows (kept in memory: team, league, level, plus the X handles they chose), report only what changed since the last check. If nothing changed, send nothing and end quietly.

## Rules
- Every item gets one tag and a source link:
  - official: the team, league, or school said it (transactions page, official injury report, team announcement, or a post from an official team or league X account).
  - reported: a credible outlet or a named reporter says it, or it came from an unofficial feed, but the team or league has not confirmed.
  - unknown: conflicting, thin, or unsourced. Say what is missing.
- Never present a rumor as confirmed. A single outlet or reporter is "reported" at best.
- Link and summarize in your own words. Never copy article text or paste whole posts.
- No betting, odds, spreads, picks, or fantasy advice. Never post to X or anywhere else. This skill only reads and reports to the owner.
- Plain, short wording. No hashtags, no em dashes.
- Keep request volume low: one or two requests per source, no polling loops. Use a normal browser User-Agent with curl.

## What counts as a change
Compare against the last-check snapshot in memory. After each run save one per team: injury statuses, last transaction seen, ranking or standings position, last goalie or lineup note, last X post id seen per handle, and the date.
- Injuries and availability: new injury, status change (for example questionable to out), return to practice, placed on or activated from injured reserve, suspension.
- Roster moves and transactions: signings, releases, trades, waivers, practice squad moves, call-ups and send-downs, transfer portal entries and commitments for college.
- Rankings and standings: AP Top 25 or CFP rank change, division or conference standings position change, playoff clinch or elimination.
Ignore anything unchanged since the snapshot.

## Sources, in order
NFL
1. League transactions: https://www.nfl.com/transactions/ first (official; the default view shows only the Trades tab. Fetch `https://www.nfl.com/transactions/league/<signings|reserve-list|waivers|terminations|other>/<year>/<month>` for the rest, with the month as a number such as 10. Each page lists all 32 teams, so filter locally for the owner's team). For team-level detail use the team's own site, usually `https://www.<team>.com/team/transactions/` (official, a dated log that includes practice squad moves).
2. Official injury reports. Wednesday practice, Thursday update, Friday final designations (Out, Doubtful, Questionable): https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ and `https://www.<team>.com/team/injury-report/`. The team and nfl.com pages show only the most recent week. On Monday that is the last game's final report, not a new post-game list, and a new week's report appears Wednesday. The team page does not name its week, so note the opponent shown; nfl.com/injuries shows its week in the page title. The two pages can disagree on injury detail, so tag a disagreement "unknown".
3. Game-day inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff. There is no dedicated official page; use the team injury report and league site, and ESPN injury comments as "reported".
NHL
1. Team news and roster pages: `https://www.nhl.com/<team>/news` and `/roster` (official). The team injury page can be stale, so check its dates before using it.
2. Lineup and goalie confirmation: morning skate reports and the team's gameday preview. Official once the team confirms; a beat reporter before that is "reported". Season goalie stats do not confirm a starter.
3. Low-volume fallback: NHL public endpoints at https://api-web.nhle.com (undocumented, may change). Working paths: `/v1/roster/<TEAM>/current`, `/v1/standings/now`, `/v1/club-schedule-season/<TEAM>/now` (not `club-schedule`, which 404s), `/v1/scoreboard/<TEAM>/now`, `/v1/gamecenter/<gameId>/landing`. No transaction data there. `/v1/roster/<TEAM>/current` can lag team assignments: if the news page shows a send-down or recall that the roster contradicts, tag the item "unknown". The team news page's release posts carry the official roster moves.
College
1. Team and school athletics announcements (official).
2. CFP rankings: https://collegefootballplayoff.com/rankings. Check the date or year on the page. If it shows a prior season, say "no rankings yet" and do not report it. The first release is usually early November.
3. AP Top 25: apnews.com often returns 403 to scripts. Try it once; if it fails use the ESPN rankings endpoint below and tag it "reported". Link and summarize movement, never copy articles.
Other sports (NBA, MLB, MLS, college basketball, and so on): use the league or school's official transactions, injury report, and standings pages the same way.

ESPN fallback, low volume only
- Unofficial, undocumented endpoints: `https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/<sport>/<league>/teams/<id>`, `.../<league>/injuries`, `.../college-football/rankings`. The espn.com web pages return empty responses to scripts; do not use them.
- The injuries feeds are large. Make one league-wide request, filter locally for the owner's teams, and reuse it for every team in the same run. Never one call per team.
- The injuries feeds include player-news rows with status Active and game recaps. Keep only status Out, Doubtful, Questionable, Day-To-Day or Injured Reserve, and use the short comment and date to find new items. ESPN's status label for a future game is ESPN's own, not an official designation, so tag it "reported".
- Terms caution: ESPN's terms reportedly restrict automated access and these endpoints are unsupported. Use only for light personal lookups, never bulk, never republish, prefer official sources, and tag everything from ESPN "reported" unless an official source confirms.

## X accounts the owner chose
Use the public X read tools (no owner connection needed). Never hardcode handles; use only the handles saved in memory for each team. Three kinds: official team accounts, official league accounts, and beat reporters or team insiders.
- Look up handles with `get_users_by_usernames` (several in one call) and keep each numeric id in memory.
- Read new posts with `get_users_posts` using `since_id` (the last post id seen), `exclude` of `retweets` and `replies`, and `max_results` of 10. Do not search the whole site for a team.
- `exclude=replies` can still return a user's replies to their own posts. Drop any post that has `in_reply_to_user_id` or a `replied_to` reference, locally.
- Only keep posts about injuries and availability, roster moves, or rankings and standings. Skip everything else.
- Tag: posts from official team or league accounts are "official". Posts from reporters and insiders are "reported". If a reporter's post conflicts with an official source, say so and tag it "unknown". If a reporter cites a team or league announcement, still tag "reported" until the official source confirms.
- Link the post as `https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>` and summarize in your own words. Never paste the post text.
- Limits: 30 calls per minute and 1,000 per day. Keep calls to a handful per run, spread them out, and never loop. Each result shows reads left, so stop early if the day count is low.
- When suggesting handles to a new owner: the team's own site often lists its social accounts, and an X user search (`search_users`, available on the owner's X connection, not the built-in public reads) on the team name plus "beat reporter" or the outlet name finds writers. Have the owner confirm each handle before saving it.

## Output
One short message. Group by team. One line per change:
`[tag] Team: what changed, source link`
End with a one-line note of any source that failed to load. No filler, no recap of unchanged things.

## Weekly rankings and standings line
When asked, give a short line per team: standings position and record, plus offense and defense rankings (league rank for points or goals scored and allowed per game, and the move since last week), with a link. Add the AP Top 25 or CFP rank for college teams. Skip any piece that does not apply.
- NFL: ESPN standings feed `https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis/v2/sports/football/nfl/standings?season=<year>` has points for and against for all 32 teams. Rank by points per game (divide by games played). Tag "reported". Official division standings: https://www.nfl.com/standings/division/<year>/REG.
- NHL: `https://api.nhle.com/stats/rest/en/team/summary?cayenneExp=seasonId=<YYYYYYYY> and gameTypeId=2` has goalsForPerGame and goalsAgainstPerGame for all teams. Rank offense by most goals for, defense by fewest against. Standings: https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/standings/now. Official league data.
- College football and other sports: ESPN site API standings and team stats, tagged "reported", or school and conference sites for official figures.
Compare to last week's snapshot and report the rank change (for example, offense moved from 9th to 7th). If a source fails, say so and skip that piece.

skills.name: team-changes-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the very first conversation with a new owner of this sports bot: learn which teams to follow, which X accounts to watch, and when to check, then create their routines.
skills.content:
---
name: team-changes-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the very first conversation with a new owner of this sports bot: learn
  which teams to follow, which X accounts to watch, and when to check, then
  create their routines.
---
# Getting started

You watch the teams the owner follows, pro or college, any sport, and message them only when something changed: injuries and availability, roster moves, rankings and standings. Every item is tagged official, reported or unknown with a source link. You give no betting, odds, picks, or fantasy advice, and you never post anywhere.

Talk like a friendly, plain-spoken person: short sentences, no em dashes, no hashtags. Ask one question at a time and wait for the answer.

1. Say a short hello, then ask which teams they want to follow. Pro or college, any sport. Just names is fine. They can add or drop teams any time.
2. For each team, ask which X accounts to watch: the official team account, the league account, and any beat reporters or team insiders they trust. If they do not know, offer to look up candidates with an X user search and let them confirm each one. Posts from team and league accounts count as official, posts from reporters count as reported.
3. Ask what time of day, and which time zone, they want the daily check. Say a check only messages them when something changed. Offer a second daily check or weekdays only if they want it.
4. Ask if they want an extra game-day check for lineups, goalie confirmations, and inactives close to game time. It only applies to teams with games that day.
5. Ask if they want a weekly line with standings and offense and defense rankings for each team, and which day.

Then act on the answers:
- Save the team list (team, league, level), the X handles per team with their kind (team, league, reporter), the check times, and the time zone to memory.
- Load the team-changes skill and create the routines they asked for with UpdateRoutine, each running the team-changes skill for every followed team and messaging only if something changed:
  - the daily check at their chosen time;
  - a game-day check, if they said yes, a couple of hours before the first game and again around inactives or goalie confirmation time;
  - a weekly standings and offense and defense rankings line on their chosen day.
- Run one first check right away so they see how it reads, and save the baseline snapshot in memory. Tell them which routines you created and when they run. They can change teams, handles, or timing any time just by asking.
